smell_validity.evidence: Context absorbs five responsibilities with natural homes elsewhere (Version parser, free sizing helpers, inline construction, trait callback, label cache). Each step is locally defensible yet accumulates into a god class. Version-parsing and sizing duplication are clearly poor; extension/label/callback absorptions are arguably legitimate coordination, leaving the healthy-design boundary slightly muddy — strong but not reference-clean.

maintenance_impact.evidence: The context is where prior device questions landed, so every new one lands there too; the prompt notes nobody can tell which construction state is authoritative and touching version behavior forces reasoning about the backend. These lasting traps force unrelated details together; removal restores long-term ownership. The effect is confined to the native backend (webgl untouched), short of architecture-level.

development_plausibility.evidence: Injected code reuses the real version parser, real GL constants, and glow's khr_fallback idiom; construction reads as capability-filling and the caching/migration drift is believable. But the cfg-duplicated parser body and `#[allow(dead_code)]` on Version::parse are slight task-shaped tells that real evolution would likely deduplicate, keeping it just short of production-level authenticity.

prompt_accuracy.evidence: Per-responsibility invariants turn the 'context does too much' request into a reliable contract: embedded/WebGL version strings parse identically, non-debug devices behave as before, the callback is torn down exactly once and only when installed, sizing equals and preserves the free helpers, public API unchanged. These fence spurious teardown, helper removal, and partial cleanup, materially reducing wrong-direction and incomplete-cleanup risk.

semantic_diversity.evidence: Five distinct purposes (version parse relocation with cfg/webgl, two-strategy extension enumeration plus probe, label cache-vs-requery at two getters, callback install/release/Drop symmetry, sizing delegation) each need a different code-supported decision: cfg path, strategy selection, cache lifetime, resource-release timing, delegation-vs-duplication. Meets 4 and each purpose needs a distinct decision.

localization_burden.evidence: Data flow crosses components (version.rs↔native.rs for the parser forward; lib.rs↔native.rs for the sizing impl). Finding the probe `supports_extension_indexing_queries` (config selection) and `install_debug_callback`/`release_debug_callback` (callback registration) is required, and plausible locations must be excluded (free pixel helpers stay; the delegating trait method is a boundary, not the smell).

repair_coordination.evidence: Callback custody and teardown timing interlock: moving install out of the context changes both the install path and Drop's release symmetry, so moving only one breaks teardown ('exactly once and only when installed'). Label cache population and the two getter reads likewise interlock. Two rules affect each other across locations; no demonstrated cross-stage silent failure beyond these interlocks.

mechanical_resistance.evidence: The best uniform operation (delegate/reconnect to an existing module authority) cleanly covers sizing accessors (delegate to free helpers) and, with a cfg wrinkle, version (reconnect Version::parse) — one to two of five responsibilities (20–40%). Extensions, label, and callback lack a pre-existing external authority, so each needs a separate relocation decision; no single uniform rule covers a majority.

behavioral_risk.evidence: Concrete wrong edits compile and pass ordinary calls but fail in special state: an unconditional Drop unregister violates 'only when installed' when no callback was set; dropping the debug gate on label re-query misbehaves on non-debug devices; an extension mis-selection fails only on pre-3.0 embedded devices. Score-4 needs test evidence of an unchecked path, absent from the four files.

recommendation_reason: Deterministic validation passed and every Quality dimension meets the retention threshold.
